narr: A trough moved southeast through the region, generating a complex of showers and storms. Numerous reports of damaging winds, a few tornadoes and flash flooding were reported with this system.
ev: Up to five inches of rain fell in about a 6 hour period causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including Highway 94 near Rhineland.
Up to four inches of rain fell in about a 6 hour period causing flash flooding. Several roads were flooded including the intersection of Highway B and West Veterans Memorial Parkway.

Widespread flash flooding was reported across the southern half of Boone County, when up to 7 inches of rain fell in a span of 6 hours. Several water rescues were reported, including one swift water rescue. Columbia firefighters rescued a man who was clinging to a tree in Bear Creek downstream of North Creasy Springs Road after his car got swept away by the swift current. They also rescued two people from a mobile home on North Hinkson Creek Road. At least an additional 10 water rescues were performed after the drivers drove into flood waters in a number of locations around the county. Numerous roads were flooded including U.S. Highway 63 at intersection with Highway 163, Nifong Boulevard at Glen Eagle Drive, Highway WW at Old Hawthorne, Creasy Springs and Bear Creek, North Route V at Barnes School Road, and U.S. Highway 40 near Midway. The rain pushed Hinkson Creek to a record high level, flooding Wilson���s Total Fitness and the Missouri Athletic Center at Forum Boulevard and closing Providence Road through midday on Friday. A section of West Dripping Springs Road was washed out due to flash flooding from Silver Fork Creek. Highway E was flooded where it crosses over Perche Creek and Route ZZ was flooded by Harmony Creek. Also, Route Y east of Ashland was closed due to flooding from Cedar Creek. No deaths or injuries were reported.
